newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $40 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $40 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open down $40 Monday on the heels of steep losses in London overnight, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures were down sharply early Monday as aggressive specualtive selling drove prices to 19-week lows. At the midday break, benchmark September was 27 stg lower at 988 stg a tonne, traded 1,012 to 988 stg.

Friday, New York cocoa futures finished firmer in light trade but well below session highs. September settled up $6 at $1,540 a tonne after ranging from $1,561 to $1,537. Second-month December ended $5 firmer at $1,588, while the back months finished up $6.
Technically, dealers pegged September support at $1,499, followed by $1,486.
The CFTC Commitments of Traders report released after Friday's close was in line with expectations, showing speculators (non-commercials and nonreportables) were net long 24,281 lots as of July 15.
In the two weeks ending July 15, non-commercial long postions fell by 6,483 lots, to 22,511 lots. Non-commercial short positions fell by 376 lots, to 3,567 lots.
Commercial long positions rose by 4,796 lots in the two weeks, to 62,072 lots, while commercial short positions fell by 4,647 lots, to 86,353 lots.
Nonreportable long positions decreased by 4,153 lots to 15,518 lots and nonreportable short positions declined by 817 lots to 10,181 lots.

The Chocolate Manufacturers Association released the U.S. 1997 second quarter early on Friday. The data U.S. cocoa grindings rose a higher-than-expected 17.54 percent compared with the same year-ago period, to 97,223 tonnes.
Most industry analysts had anticipated the data to show a rise of between five and 10 percent.
